question: Standard (universal) precautions in an obstetric setting require gloves and eye protection to be worn during normal vaginal delivery ONLY if the patient is known to be HIV-positive or hepatitis B-positive.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. Standard precautions are applied universally — not selectively based on known serostatus. All blood and body fluids must be treated as potentially infectious during every delivery. Selective precautions based on known HIV/HBV status are both legally and clinically inadequate.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct, the statement is false. Standard precautions apply to ALL patients regardless of known infectious status. The underlying principle is that infection status is not always known; treating every patient's blood and body fluids as potentially infectious prevents both patient-to-staff and patient-to-patient transmission.
